name: eth
description: Write, test, share and deploy Ethereum smart contracts — a Solidity bench with a real editor, projects stored in the store module and identified by CID (sharing a contract is handing somebody a CID), a test runner that deploys to a testnet and asserts against real receipts, plus keystore accounts, balances, transfers, ERC-20s and event logs across 14 EVM chains. One engine behind four faces: a console, a REST API, a CLI and 42 MCP tools. Compiles with solc it finds or fetches, records every ABI against its address, and refuses to spend on a non-testnet chain without an explicit confirm.
frontend: app/server.py (stdlib — the console at /eth on :50731; proxies /eth/_api to the API)

engine.chains.py: the network registry — 14 built-in EVM chains, owner-added ones, env overrides
engine.wallet.py: keystore-v3 accounts namespaced by the signing address; bounded in-memory unlocks
engine.compiler.py: solc over standard JSON — found on the box or fetched and checksummed
engine.catalog.py: the nine shipped contract templates, described from their own source
engine.ledger.py: sqlite: deployments, attached ABIs, and every transaction this module sent
engine.ops.py: the chain operations themselves — every face calls these
engine.store_link.py: the bridge to the store module — every call carries the CALLER'S token, so the store's whitelist, quota and terms apply to whoever asked
engine.projects.py: contract projects: bytes to the store (a CID per version), an index here
engine.harness.py: the test runner — deploy to a chain, send real transactions, assert on what came back

/status.docs: Default network reachability, solc versions, templates, auth mode, and the caller's accounts when a token is sent

/me.docs: Caller address, owner flag, accounts, live unlocks and index counts

/networks.docs: The chain registry; ?check=1 pings each. POST adds a custom rpc, DELETE removes one

/accounts.docs: GET your accounts; POST creates one (or imports with `secret`)

/accounts/{name}/unlock.docs: Hold the key in memory for a bounded ttl

/accounts/{name}/export.docs: The raw private key — password plus confirm=true

/accounts/{name}/keystore.docs: The encrypted keystore file, safe to back up

/sign.docs: EIP-191 personal_sign with one of your accounts

/verify.docs: Recover the address behind a message signature

/balance.docs: Native or ERC-20 balance of an address, account name or ENS name

/portfolio.docs: Your accounts across several chains at once

/block.docs: A block by number, hash or tag

/tx.docs: A transaction and its receipt (?wait=1 to block until mined)

/gas.docs: Base fee, tip, max fee and what a plain transfer costs right now

/nonce.docs: Pending and confirmed nonce for an address

/code.docs: Is there a contract there, and is its ABI known

/logs.docs: Event logs, decoded when the ABI is known

/estimate.docs: Gas and cost for a transaction, without sending it

/send.docs: Send the native currency; confirm=true required off a testnet

/templates.docs: The nine shipped contracts; /templates/{name} for ABI, constructor and source

/compile.docs: Solidity in, ABI + bytecode out. Nothing is sent anywhere

/deploy.docs: Compile and deploy in one step; the ABI is recorded against the address

/contracts.docs: GET your deployments and attached ABIs; POST attaches an ABI to an address

/contracts/{address}.docs: GET the interface (reads, writes, events); DELETE forgets the row

/contracts/{address}/write.docs: A state-changing call; confirm=true required off a testnet

/tokens/{address}.docs: ERC-20 metadata, plus a holder balance with ?holder=

/tokens/{address}/approve.docs: Set an ERC-20 allowance ('max' for unlimited)

/history.docs: Every transaction this module sent for you, and how each ended

/mcp.docs: MCP. GET is the whole schema as a document; POST is the Streamable HTTP JSON-RPC 2.0 transport

/mcp/tools.docs: Just the tools: name, description, inputSchema, annotations, auth

/mcp/config.docs: Client config for this deployment, with the url as the caller reached it

/projects.docs: GET your contract projects (with the store's view of you); POST creates one — the bytes go to the store and the CID comes back. `origin_cid` on the body records the CID a copy came from

/projects/{project}.docs: One project by id, slug or CID. PUT saves a new version (a new CID; the old one still resolves). DELETE drops it here, and from the store only with ?from_store=true

/projects/{project}/share.docs: Publish it in the store. The CID is the share link

/projects/{project}/unshare.docs: Make it private again — anyone already holding the CID keeps what they fetched

/open.docs: Read a shared project out of the store by CID. No account needed for a public one

/fork.docs: Copy a shared project into your own workspace, recording where it came from

/store.docs: Where storage stands for you: is the store up, may you upload, have you signed its terms, quota left

/store/terms.docs: Sign-accept the store's terms with your own token

/test.docs: Deploy to a chain and run a suite against it — real transactions, real receipts. Refuses a non-testnet without confirm=true. The report is stored and gets a CID

/test/generate.docs: A starter suite read off the ABI — every zero-argument getter, no invented expectations

/tests/{run_id}.docs: One run in full — every case and the hash behind each write

safety.mainnet: any write on a chain with testnet=false is refused unless the request carries confirm=true — an argument, not a setting
safety.estimation: every write is gas-estimated first, so a transaction that would revert is never broadcast
safety.keys: keystore-v3, scrypt, namespaced by the signing address; usable only while unlocked or when the password is supplied
safety.scoping: accounts and the deployment index are private per address; an ABI looked up by address is not, because an interface is public

transports.http: POST /mcp on the API — schema at GET /mcp
transports.stdio: python3 mcp.py — runs as this box's own identity

mcp.auth: the caller's mod-protocol token as Authorization: Bearer; every read tool needs none

env.ETH_DIR: State dir: accounts, sqlite index, solc cache, networks (default ~/.mod/eth)
env.ETH_RPC_<NAME>: Override one chain's rpc, e.g. ETH_RPC_MAINNET=https://…/v2/<key>
env.ETH_RPC_TIMEOUT: Seconds to wait on an rpc call (default 30)
env.ETH_PRIVATE_KEY: A key exposed as the account 'env' — for a headless box that is deliberately trusted
env.ETH_MAX_UNLOCK: Ceiling on an unlock ttl in seconds (default 900)
env.ETH_SOLC_DOWNLOAD: 0 = never fetch a compiler; only use what is on the box
env.ETH_WAIT_TIMEOUT: Default seconds to wait for a receipt (default 180)
env.ETH_OPEN: 1 = treat every caller as one local identity (local development only)
env.ETH_OWNER: Fallback owner address when ~/.mod/eth/owner.json is absent

state: ~/.mod/eth — accounts/ (keystore v3), eth.db (sqlite), networks.json, owner.json, solc/

storage.what: project bundles (sources + suites) and every test report, as JSON objects addressed by CID
storage.auth: the caller's own mod-protocol token, forwarded verbatim — this module holds no store credentials and cannot reach an object the caller could not
storage.fallback: a project the store refuses is still kept in the local index with its bytes cached; it has no CID and cannot be shared until the store accepts it
